records.scope: First five season-two released guide entries (six numbered parts): 100 selected profiles, named official narrative/trivia evidence and direct/remote distinctions. Original-US date policy retained. No release, edition, credit or episode-inventory changes.
limitations: The first five season-two guide entries (six numbered parts) now have selected reviews against 100 profiles. The Siege of Lothal remains one combined guide. All fourteen first-season guides retain their 217 connections. Nineteen of 66 Rebels guide entries are now reviewed; 47 guides / 54 numbered parts remain pending. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent.

Lando’s Siege hologram, the Emperor’s ending contact and Sato’s generator briefing are transmissions. Tua and Kallus retain direct rows when actual scenes accompany remote contact. Force sensing does not replace the actual physical scenes of Ahsoka, Kanan and Vader.

The modified Seelos walker, legacy AT-TE family, AT-AT family and distinct episode variant are scoped separately. The abandoned medical station shares a design with Kaliida Shoals but is not identified as that station. Nixus Hub 218, Tarkintown and the medical station are places, not additional planets. A single Ghost/Phantom caption inconsistency is explained, not copied into an unsupported ship location.

Trayvis’s vision, broadcast and physical meeting share one direct row with context. Alton/Trayvis interviews, Fulcrum’s remote conversation and Bail’s holographic greeting are transmissions. Ahsoka’s finale reveal and Vader’s Lothal arrival are direct scenes; later Kallus-Fulcrum biography is not assigned to the season-one contact.

The Sovereign, communications light-cruiser family, stolen rescue transport, Broken Horn and two distinct stolen/borrowed TIEs retain separate identities and scope. Mustafar is only a planned destination in Rebel Resolve but a system setting in the finale. No Gideon/Trask hull, generic Lambda, A-wing or technical metadata inferred.

Path of the Jedi distinguishes nightmare visions from direct scenes and Yoda’s remote communication through the Force. Mixed direct/vision contexts use one direct row with explanation; no real crew deaths or physical Yoda temple visit are asserted.

Fort Anaxes is the Rebels-era asteroid base. The displayed parade TIE and Inquisitor’s pursuit fighter are distinct. The Relentless has no assumed subclass and the landing shuttle has no assumed Lambda/Theta identity. No legacy technical fields inherited.

The combined Spark of Rebellion guide remains one review for parts 1–2. The later ABC Vader opening is excluded from original-pilot connections and remains a distinct documented version. No scene is assigned to an individual pilot part without evidence.

Obi-Wan’s holocron message, Trayvis’s broadcast and Luminara’s projected bait are transmissions. Luminara’s remains are also shown. Remote contacts followed by physical scenes use a single direct row with context; mentions, aliases and repeated names are not extra characters.
Episode inventory and writing credits do not establish every language mix, supplied master or frame-level version. Public references are not open media licences.

Normalized count: 75 numbered parts across four seasons (15/22/22/16), grouped into 66 official guide entries (14/20/19/13). This is an archive counting convention, not a universal count of playable streaming items. The four introductory shorts and the ABC revised pilot are excluded. Individual credits and appearances within combined parts are not inferred.

Current release-date research is restricted to the original US launch of each work and, when necessary to distinguish a documented version, its first US release. Existing sourced events are retained. Worldwide/Finland dates, later platform availability, routine rereleases and exhaustive master comparisons are deferred rather than factually resolved.

Captions 2, 4–5 / named AT-AT and distinct model

episodeReviews.scope: One released guide entry reviewed against 100 selected profiles using named official narrative/trivia evidence. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. Direct scenes and transmissions are distinguished. The combined Siege guide covers parts 1–2 without unsupported part-level allocation.
notes: The official guide and its 41-image gallery cover both parts. Trivia caption 1 explicitly says production episodes 201 and 202 were developed together. This review creates one combined entry, not an invented split of characters between the two parts.

Lando’s hologram is visually verified in official narrative image 28; he is not physically at the farm. The Emperor is contacted remotely in the ending. Tua has a remote request and later actual dock scenes, so her combined row is direct. Ahsoka, Kanan and Vader also connect through the Force but all have actual scenes, so one direct row per identity is retained.

Tarkin is referred to but not established in person by the selected evidence. Anakin is Vader’s former name, not a second character physically present. Pryce and Morad Sumar belong to discarded outlines described in trivia, not released-scene links. Mustafar is a reference to the previous victory, not a current setting.

The Phoenix Home is a named Pelta-class frigate, distinct from later blockade-runner command ships. Vader’s TIE Advanced is distinct from the Grand Inquisitor’s prototype. Unspecified shuttles, walkers and spy droids are not assigned legacy Lambda, Sentinel, AT-DP or probe-droid identities without model evidence.

notes: The Fifth Brother and Seventh Sister are distinct hunters. The Grand Inquisitor is discussed and his weapon design compared, but neither makes him a physical station visitor. Ahsoka is an interrogation target and later reported upon, not established in person by these sources.
Admiral Konstantine is explicitly named in trivia caption 3 for his actual complaints about the Inquisitor. Admiral Motti and Ozzel are comparisons to film officers, not new episode appearances.

The unnamed abandoned station is not declared to be Kaliida Shoals: trivia caption 5 establishes a shared design only. The profile uses a descriptive editorial label and is classified as a space station, not a planet.

Narrative caption 24 calls the escape vessel the Ghost, but captions 23, 26 and 28 consistently identify it as the Phantom, which returns to the Ghost. The Ghost link is supported by the opening and ending, not an unsupported station visit. No separate second escape ship is invented.
Zeb’s Commander Meiloorun transmission is a disguise by the same character, not an additional commander. Rex’s recollection of his Jedi general does not add Anakin as a current scene or flashback.

Ezra calls himself Lando Calrissian; this does not create a Lando appearance. Hondo’s past Jedi contacts, the jacket symbol’s later film use and Azmorigan’s Jabba-inspired design likewise do not create those character appearances.

Nixus Hub 218 is explicitly named by trivia caption 2. Azmorigan’s yacht is described in trivia as a SoroSuub design derived from Lady Luck concept history; this does not identify it as Lady Luck or the previously profiled Merchant One.

Sabine, Hera, Kanan and Rex are explicitly named at the reunion. Zeb is not individually established in these selected captions, so that link remains unestablished. A named crew collective alone does not corroborate every member.
